newsitem.title: JAPAN: French president wants an active Japan-report.
newsitem.headline: French president wants an active Japan-report.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, on the eve of a six-day to Japan, said in an interview published on Saturday that France wants Tokyo to play a more active role in international affairs.
"In a period of world crisis France looks to Japan as an important player to consult with," Chirac told the Asahi Shimbun newspaper.
In talks with Japanese premier Ryutaro Hashimoto on Monday, Chirac is expected to ask for Japanese help in handling the refugee crisis in Zaire.
Chirac recently called for intervention by a "politically neutral" multinational force" to deliver food and medical aid to hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded in eastern Zaire.

The Franco-Japanese summit is intended to "restore" bilateral relations, according to Japanese officials, after Japanese public outrage exploded at France's South Pacific nuclear tests which began in September last year.
Chirac said in the interview with the Asahi that he had closed down a nuclear fissile material production facility used by the French military in southern France.
He reiterated France's support for a ban on the production of fissile material, the raw material for nuclear warheads.

Since the end of the Mururoa undersea blasts, France has been promoting the signing of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT). It has vigorously advocated nuclear disarmament and opposed developing nations' attempts to create their own nuclear arsenals.
Two possible bones of contention likely to surface during the summit talks are China's participation in coming G7 talks and the opening of the Japanese market.
"The preconditions for participation in the (G7) talks are democracy and a free market," the French president told the Asahi, underlining his opposition to China's participation.
France is expected to seek the opening up of the Japanese insurance, construction, aircraft and car manufacturing industries to French companies.
